footer.aboutTitle: About This Quick Nursing Knowledge Challenge
footer.aboutText: This nursing knowledge quiz is inspired by broad thinking skills used in safe, respectful patient care, including hygiene, observation, privacy, identity checks, medicine checks, and urgent priorities. It is for entertainment and curiosity only, not a nursing qualification, clinical assessment, medical advice, or official training exam.

stageGroups.title: Safety Basics
stageGroups.encouragement: Good start. Your first nursing score is locked in.

questions.prompt: A nurse washes hands before and after care. What is the main purpose?
A patient says they feel dizzy when standing. What is the safest first response?
choices: Ask them to sit or stay steady
Ignore it because it may pass

questions.prompt: Which action best protects privacy?
choices: Discuss care in a private place
Leave notes open on a table

questions.prompt: Before helping someone move, what should be checked first?
choices: Whether the hallway music is loud

questions.prompt: Which moment calls for hand hygiene?
choices: Only at the start of a shift

questions.prompt: A curtain is open during personal care. What is the best first action?
A patient uses a walking aid. What is the safest approach?
choices: Keep it available if they need it

questions.prompt: Gloves are worn for a task. What still matters?
choices: Using the same gloves all day

questions.prompt: A visitor asks about another patient nearby. What should happen?
Which choice sounds most like safe basic care?

stageGroups.title: Care Checks
stageGroups.encouragement: Solid focus. The next round moves into priority decisions.

questions.prompt: Why is a patient identity check important before care?
choices: It helps match care to the right person

questions.prompt: A reading is very different from the previous one. What is a wise first step?
choices: Check the reading again if safe

questions.prompt: A patient says a tablet looks different from usual. What should happen?
Which detail is best before recording a measurement?
choices: That the reading belongs to the right person

questions.prompt: A number on a monitor seems surprising. What is the safest mindset?
choices: Recheck and use the proper process
Tell everyone it is definitely wrong

questions.prompt: A medicine label and chart do not seem to match. What is the best response?
Someone asks for details over the phone. What matters most first?
choices: The request is verified through the right process

questions.prompt: A patient gives a different name than expected. What should happen?
A recorded reading has a missing digit. What is the careful response?
choices: Clarify or repeat the reading if appropriate

questions.prompt: Which action protects confidentiality best?
choices: Discussing details quietly in the correct setting

questions.prompt: A patient is usually alert but is suddenly very confused. What matters most?
choices: It is a change from normal

questions.prompt: A family member asks for private information in a public area. What is the best response?
choices: Move to a suitable process or private setting
Ignore privacy because they asked nicely

questions.prompt: A patient asks for help, but another patient has an emergency. What is the best approach?
choices: Address the emergency and arrange support for the other need
Help only the person who asked first

questions.prompt: A patient suddenly becomes short of breath while another asks for a blanket. What should happen first?
Which change should be taken seriously?
Two needs happen at once: pain report and spilled water near a walking path. What is the best thinking?
choices: Prioritize immediate safety while arranging care

questions.prompt: A patient’s breathing looks suddenly harder than before. What is the safest priority?
choices: Treat it as urgent and get appropriate help
Wait until the room is tidy

questions.prompt: A calm patient suddenly becomes hard to wake. What is the key clue?
Which situation should usually come before routine comfort requests?
A patient says, “I can’t catch my breath.” What is the best first priority?
choices: Respond promptly and follow the proper care process
Ask them to wait until later
Tell them it is probably nothing
